findings.issue: Fail-open is not preserved for contract load/read failures. resolveAgent converts an unavailable/failed dispatch contract into expected inline with proven:false; then any subprocess actual shape becomes a high-severity unproven-subprocess mismatch and shapeDoor refuses under enforce. I simulated contract unavailable and legitimate backend-builder/backend-reviewer subprocess dispatches returned action:"refuse".
findings.fix: Treat resolver dependency failures as true fail-open in shapeDoor. For example, have resolveAgent throw a sentinel caught by shapeDoor, or mark source:"fail-open" mismatches as proceed/non-high before the enforce check.

findings.issue: WARPOS_SHAPE_DOOR=report is not an absolute fleet kill when WARPOS_DISPATCH_CONTRACT_ENFORCE=block is also present. The legacy block alias wins and mode becomes enforce, so a stale legacy env can override the operator's explicit report kill.
findings.fix: Check globalRaw === "report" before legacyBlock, or make legacyBlock apply only when WARPOS_SHAPE_DOOR is unset. Add a regression for report+legacyBlock.

findings.issue: The per-wrapper "kill" env only sets enforceDefault:false; it does not force report if WARPOS_SHAPE_DOOR=enforce or the legacy block env is set. That is weaker than the documented per-wrapper kill escape.
findings.fix: If the wrapper env is report/off/0, pass a real report pin/force-report option to shapeDoor, or document it as only disabling the default flip, not as a kill.

findings.issue: Tests cover thrown resolver errors and simple escapes, but not the non-throwing contract-unavailable fail-open path, not report+legacyBlock precedence, and not per-wrapper kill behavior under global enforce.
findings.fix: Add child-process tests with WARPOS_DISPATCH_CONTRACT_PATH pointing at a bad/missing file, WARPOS_SHAPE_DOOR=report plus WARPOS_DISPATCH_CONTRACT_ENFORCE=block, and wrapper env report combined with global enforce.

parsed.summary: Normal registered-role routing looks safe: cross-provider reviewers and build-chain roles resolve proven:true to the matching wrapper shape, and dispatch-claude still passes sanctioned:fallbackSanctioned so the review-fallback lane is suppressed/proceeds. However, the enforce flip is not blast-safe because resolver dependency failures can become high refusals, and two documented report escapes are not absolute under conflicting envs.
